name: IR21814STRPBF
title: IR2181 / IR21814: 600 V high- and low-side gate driver, 1.4 A / 1.8 A
summary: A two-channel gate driver for N-channel MOSFETs and IGBTs: one channel referred to ground and one floating channel, bootstrap powered, that works with its return up to +600 V. Each output follows its own logic input (3.3 V and 5 V compatible), with no interlock or dead time, and the two propagation delays are matched within 35 ns. Both supplies have undervoltage lockout. The IR2181 comes in 8-lead PDIP and SOIC; the IR21814 adds a separate logic ground, VSS, in 14-lead PDIP and SOIC.
key_figures: 600 V (VS recommended max), VB 625 V abs max
VCC and VBS 10 V to 20 V
1.4 A source / 1.8 A sink min; 1.9 A / 2.3 A typ
VIH 2.7 V min, VIL 0.8 V max

circuits.title: Typical connection, IR2181
circuits.description: An 8-lead IR2181 drives one half bridge of N-channel MOSFETs from a rail of up to 600 V. VCC feeds the low side directly and charges the bootstrap capacitor C2 between VB and VS through the diode D1 whenever the low MOSFET pulls VS to ground. HO and LO each drive a gate through a series resistor. The switch node, VS and the high MOSFET's source, goes to the load. C1 decouples VCC to COM, and C3 decouples the high-voltage rail to ground.
notes: Q1's source and Q2's drain go to the load on separate leads.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IR21814
circuits.description: A 14-lead IR21814 drives one half bridge of N-channel MOSFETs from a rail of up to 600 V, with its logic ground VSS brought out apart from the power return COM. C1 decouples VCC to VSS at the logic side and C3 decouples VCC to COM. D1 charges the bootstrap capacitor C2 between VB and VS from VCC. HO and LO drive the gates through series resistors, COM returns to the low MOSFET's source, and C4 decouples the high-voltage rail to that ground.
notes: Q1's source and Q2's drain go to the load on separate leads.

operation.text: Two independent gate drivers for N-channel power MOSFETs or IGBTs: a low-side channel referred to COM and a floating high-side channel that rides on VS and may sit up to 600 V above COM. The high side is meant to be powered by a bootstrap supply. Output stages source 1.4 A and sink 1.8 A (minimum pulsed), with drive edges slowed (lower di/dt) for noise immunity.

HIN and LIN take standard CMOS or LSTTL levels down to 3.3 V logic (VIH 2.7 V min, VIL 0.8 V max). Each output follows its own input in phase (HO with HIN, LO with LIN); there is no cross-conduction logic and no dead time in the IR2181/IR21814. A 5.2 V zener clamps each input inside the part.
The 14-lead IR21814 brings out VSS, the logic ground, apart from COM, the power return; VSS may be offset ±5 V from COM. On the 8-lead IR2181 the logic is referred to COM.
Both VCC and VBS have undervoltage lockout. The rising threshold is 8.0 V to 9.8 V (8.9 V typ), the falling threshold 7.4 V to 9.0 V (8.2 V typ), with 0.3 V minimum hysteresis.

HIN passes through an input level shifter referred to VSS/COM and a pulse generator; a high-voltage level shifter carries the pulses up to the floating side, where a pulse filter sets and resets a latch that drives HO. The floating side has its own UV detect block.
LIN passes through an input level shifter and a delay stage to LO; the low side has its own UV detect block on VCC. Delay matching between the two channels is 35 ns max.
The logic keeps working with VS from -5 V up to +600 V and tolerates negative transients on VS; for VS between -5 V and -VBS the output state is held. The offset may slew at up to 50 V/ns.

Turn-on delay ton runs from the input's 50 % point on its rising edge to the output's 10 % point; rise time tr is the output's 10 % to 90 %. Turn-off delay toff runs from the input's 50 % point on its falling edge to the output's 90 % point; fall time tf is the output's 90 % to 10 %. Delay matching MT is the gap between the LO and HO edges for the same input edge, at 10 % on turn-on and 90 % on turn-off.

The temperature of IR2181, IR21814, IR2181S and IR21814S rises with switching frequency over 1 kHz to 1 MHz when driving IRFBC20 (33 Ω gate resistor), IRFBC30 (22 Ω), IRFBC40 (15 Ω) or IRFPE50 (10 Ω) at VCC = 15 V, with curves for 0 V, 70 V and 140 V.

The top marking carries the part number, a date code YWW followed by a marking code (P for a lead-free part, blank for non-lead-free), the IR logo, a pin-1 dot, and a lot code: an assembly site code (per SCOP 200-002) and a 4-digit SPN code.
Designed and qualified for industrial use.
